exposure: Cervical ripening method (dinoprostone vs Foley catheter)
cohort: 238 patients with term prelabor rupture of membranes (TPROM) after 37 weeks of gestation requiring cervical ripening
finding: Cervical ripening with a Foley catheter in cases of TPROM after 37 weeks of gestation appears to be as safe as prostaglandins regarding the mode of delivery, although it results in a longer induction to delivery interval and labor duration.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference between the dinoprostone and Foley catheter groups regarding the rate of cesarean section.
